The idea is simple: each star chart is a decade of logged nightly observations plus a signed observatory record, so a farm must grind a hundred real lenses by hand, and that meadow alone separates one real agent from a hundred fakes. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The lantern is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red. The wharf is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
